cases.ask: What is the trend of Navaneeth taking leave?
cases.reference: States first that the last six months were analysed, with the dates; then days taken and requests, by type, the patterns, the change against the six months before, and only the Notable lines as highlights. Counts and dates only — no reason, motive or judgement, no comparison with anyone else. Cites the result.

cases.ask: Show me Navaneeth's leave trend over the last 12 months.
cases.reference: Two cards laid out with present from the result's own figures (EC-D274): a figures card titled 'Leave trend · Navaneeth …', subtitled with the period and the Pattern line, its five tiles in order (Leave taken, Requests, Monday or Friday, Long breaks, Leave left); then a 'By month' table with a row a month, a column a leave type and a Total row. Every figure exactly as the result writes it. The words: one sentence naming the person and the period, the Notable lines, upcoming leave — never the cards' figures again.

cases.ask: How has Navaneeth's leave looked over the last quarter?
cases.reference: The last full quarter, named with its dates, against the quarter before. Not the default six months.

cases.ask: What does my leave pattern look like this year?
cases.reference: The asker's own leave this year so far, against the same days of last year.

One short message asking only for the employee code, the designation (the HRMS's designations as choices), the date of joining and a phone number, and their personal email (where the setup email goes). Never the name or company email again, never the status, never the company when there is only one, never PAN, Aadhaar or bank details.

cases.ask: Onboard Ethan Parker ethanparker@hamon.in, employee code H901, Software Engineer, joining 2026-12-01, phone 9876543210
cases.reference: Straight to the create_employee card for Confirm, carrying exactly what HR said: no question back, and no 'shall I go ahead?' of its own.

ask: Code H901, Software Engineer, joining 2026-12-01, phone 9876543210
cases.reference: The second message completes the record: the card carries the name and email from the first and the rest from the second, with nothing asked again.

cases.ask: Onboard Ethan Parker ethanparker@hamon.in, employee code H901, Software Engineer, joining 2026-12-01, phone 9876543210, PAN ABCDE1234F
cases.reference: The card carries no PAN (the tool takes none); the answer says the employee adds it on their own profile, without repeating the number.
A question back, asking for the company email at hamon.in. Does not take the Gmail address as the company email.
Each new employee waiting, with the times they are free (date and time), or that none is waiting. Reads only; cites the result.

cases.ask: Confirm Ethan Parker's orientation for 2026-12-02 at 11:00
cases.reference: Asks, in one short question, where it is (a room or a meeting link). Never guesses a place, and proposes nothing yet.

cases.ask: Confirm Ethan Parker's orientation for 2026-12-02 at 11:00 in Room 2
cases.reference: Straight to the confirm_orientation card for Confirm, carrying exactly what HR said: no question back, and no 'shall I go ahead?' of its own.

One short line per person being onboarded: name, progress and the step they are on, with what needs HR after it when there is something; or that nobody is. Never an internal step key or an id. Cites the result.

A first line with the name, the progress and when it started; then the steps in order, each with its status in plain words and any note or error; the orientation and latest reminders only if there are any. Steps by their names, never their keys.
Straight to the retry card for Confirm, with HR's words for the person and the step passed as said; no question back and no 'shall I go ahead?'.

cases.ask: Ethan Parker is on an internal project, so mark Jira not required for him
cases.reference: The not-required card for Confirm, carrying HR's reason as given; the bot does not ask for one.

cases.ask: Mark Ethan Parker's profile as confirmed
cases.reference: Says a step is completed only when it is verified, so it cannot be marked done from chat, and offers what can be done (for example that the employee confirms their profile, or that HR can mark the step not required). Proposes no card.
